referents.why: 'his hand' in the clause 'Aaron stretched out his hand' is Aaron's; masculine singular agrees and Aaron is the doer of the act.
'his staff' is Aaron's, the staff he stretches out; same doer.
'they did so' is plural and fulfils the command chain, which was addressed to Moses (to tell) and Aaron (to act); the composite Moses and Aaron is the only plural candidate that fits.
referents.category: plural they fulfilling a command chain

referents.why: 'he struck the dust' continues Aaron's acts in cl1 with no change of subject; the implied subject is Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject of a series of acts

cant_tell.what: whether cl3 or cl4 is the fulfilment of the command's effect, or both
cant_tell.why: both repeat the verb hayah of the effect; both are recorded as fulfilling it, and the split between the gnats on man and beast (result of the striking) and the all-dust summary is not settled by the text.
the gloss gives a feminine singular verb while the gnats are masculine; no slot depends on it, since the subject is named as the gnats.
